title: Shopify Store Navigation — Menus, Nesting & Implementation
content: Official Shopify navigation guidelines (from shopify.dev). Themes access store navigation through the linklists object. Merchants create menus in Online Store > Navigation in admin. Default menu: 'Main menu' accessed via main-menu handle. MENU STRUCTURE: Three levels of hierarchy supported: (1) Primary links — section.settings.menu.links. (2) Child links — link.links attribute. (3) Grandchild links — child_link.links. Each link object contains title and url properties. MERCHANT CONTROL: Use link_list setting type to let merchants select which menu displays in any section. PLACEMENT: Navigation code goes in header or footer sections. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Design navigation with three levels of depth. Level 1: main horizontal nav bar items. Level 2: dropdown menu items (triggered on hover/click). Level 3: nested submenu items (flyout or indented within dropdown). Design both the desktop horizontal nav and mobile hamburger menu states. For desktop mega-menus, design a full-width dropdown panel that can accommodate multiple columns of links (Level 2 items as column headers, Level 3 items as column links). For footer navigation, design 3–4 columns of link lists. Always include: logo (links to home), main nav, search icon, cart icon with count badge, and account icon in the header.

title: Shopify Storefront Search — Query Parameters, Predictive Search & Results
content: Official Shopify search guidelines (from shopify.dev). Search is based on query parameters that customise what returns and how results display. QUERY PARAMETERS: Required: q (search query string). Optional: type (filter by resource — product, page, article; defaults to all), page (results page, defaults to 1), options (hash for customisation), unavailable_products (show, hide, or last — controls out-of-stock display), prefix (partial word matching on final term — 'last' or 'none'), sort_by (relevance, price-ascending, price-descending). SEARCH FORM: Use <form> with action='/search'. Include visible input for query and hidden inputs for parameters. PARTIAL WORD MATCHING: Enables 'winter snow' to match 'snowshoe' or 'snowboard'. UNAVAILABLE PRODUCTS: Three options — show (display normally), hide (exclude from results), last (push to end of results). PREDICTIVE SEARCH: Separate feature showing suggestions while typing. MULTI-LANGUAGE: Use routes object for correct URL population. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Design four search states: (1) Search icon in header — default state. (2) Search overlay/modal when activated — full-width input field with close button, recent searches list, and trending searches. (3) Predictive search dropdown — shows product thumbnails, page titles, and collection matches as user types, with loading skeleton state. (4) Search results page — product grid with sort dropdown, filter sidebar, result count, and empty state for no results. Design the sort options: Relevance, Price Low-High, Price High-Low, Newest. Design how unavailable products appear differently from available ones (dimmed image, 'Sold out' badge).

title: Shopify Storefront Filtering — Methods, Types & UX Patterns
content: Official Shopify filtering guidelines (from shopify.dev). Two filtering methods: (1) Storefront filtering (recommended) — merchants establish filter groups using existing product data. Supports filtering by availability, price, variant options, and additional criteria. Applies to both collections and search results. (2) Tag filtering — uses product tags to segment collections into smaller subsets. Alternative when storefront filtering is not implemented. FILTER TYPES: Availability (in stock / out of stock), price range (min/max slider or inputs), variant options (size, colour, material — based on product options), product type, vendor, and custom metafield filters. FIGMA IMPLICATION: Design two filter layouts: (1) Desktop sidebar filter — 240–280px wide left panel with collapsible filter groups. Each group has a header (e.g. 'Size', 'Colour', 'Price') and expandable content. Checkbox-style for multi-select filters (size, colour). Min/max inputs or range slider for price. Show active filter count per group. 'Clear all' link at top. (2) Mobile filter drawer — slides in from bottom or right. Same filter groups but in a full-screen or half-screen drawer. 'Apply' and 'Clear' buttons at bottom. Active filter count on the trigger button ('Filter (3)'). ACTIVE FILTERS: Design as removable chips/pills above the product grid — each chip shows the filter value and an × to remove. Include a 'Clear all filters' link. FILTER RESULT COUNT: Show product count updating as filters are applied ('24 products' → '8 products'). Design the empty state when filters return zero results — friendly message with suggestion to broaden filters.
